item.title: NHC Foods expands portfolio with Sachmaas acquisition; Q2 net up 16 times
item.description: NHC Foods Ltd, an exporter of agricultural commodities and spices, reported a sharp improvement in financial performance for the September quarter, with total income rising 333 per cent year-on-year to Rs 451.32 crore and profit surging more than 16-fold to Rs 21.68 crore. The company had reported total income of Rs 104.09 crore and profit of Rs 1.34 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year, according to a company statement. For the first half of FY27, NHC Foods posted total income of Rs 821.45 crore, an increase of 282 per cent from Rs 214.68 crore a year earlier. Profit rose nearly 13-fold to Rs 38.68 crore, compared with Rs 3.01 crore in the year-ago period. Commenting on the performance, Managing Director Satyam Joshi said, "We are encouraged by the strong performance this quarter and in the first half and remain focused on sustaining this growth momentum. Our strategy is centred on expanding our operations, strengthening our presence in the agri ...

item.title: Manappuram Finance Q2 results: Profit jumps over 3-fold to ₹701 crore
item.description: Gold loan financier Manappuram Finance Ltd on Thursday reported a more than three-fold year-on-year increase in its consolidated profit after tax (PAT) to Rs 701 crore for the September quarter of FY27. The company had posted a PAT of Rs 217.31 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal. On a sequential basis, net profit rose 20 per cent from Rs 585 crore in the June quarter. Total income increased to Rs 3,312 crore in the second quarter of FY27, compared to Rs 2,275 crore in the year-ago period, the company said in a regulatory filing. The company's total assets under management (AUM) stood at Rs 73,303 crore as of September 2026, registering a year-on-year growth of 60 per cent. Gold Loan AUM surged 92.5 per cent YoY to Rs 60,640 crore at the end of the September quarter. Shares of Manappuram Finance settled 0.23 per cent lower at Rs 320.25 apiece on the BSE.

item.title: Tata Projects-led JV wins Dhaka Metro contract for 5.2-km underground line
item.description: Tata Projects on Thursday said the company, along with Japanese firms Nishimatsu Construction and Toda Corporation, has bagged an order to build an underground section of the Dhaka Metro, further expanding its global urban transit footprint. The project encompasses civil works, including architectural finishes and mechanical, electrical, and plumbing systems, for the construction of a 5.2-km underground main line. It also includes three underground stations -- Khilkhet, Airport Terminal-3, and Airport -- along with a shaft at the northern end. "Tata Projects Limited (TPL), as part of the Nishimatsu-TPL-Toda Joint Venture, has secured Contract Package CP06 from Dhaka Mass Transit Company Limited (DMTCL) for a key section of the Dhaka Metro network in Bangladesh," the company said in a statement. item.title: HFCL bags export orders worth ₹834 crore for optical fibre cables
item.description: Telecom gear maker HFCL on Thursday said it has secured export orders worth about Rs 834.36 crore (around USD 88.94 million) for supplying optical fibre cables to an international customer, through its overseas wholly-owned subsidiary. The order is scheduled for completion by June 2027. The company, however, did not disclose the identity of the customer. "These orders reaffirm the confidence reposed by our customers in the company's manufacturing capabilities, technological excellence and product quality," HFCL said in a regulatory filing. HFCL posted a multi-fold jump in consolidated profit to Rs 394.22 crore in the second quarter ended September 30, 2026, up from Rs 72 crore a year ago, driven by demand for optical fibre cables from AI data centres. The company has forecasted 80 per cent revenue growth in FY27 and expects to achieve the Rs 10,000 crore revenue mark before the projected timeline of FY29. HFCL's consolidated revenue from operations more than doubled to Rs 2,541.7
